title: Deconfounding Game 4: M-bias
content: Smoking and lung disease are unconfounded in the M-graph until seat-belt usage is conditioned upon. Seat-belt usage is a collider reflecting two distinct attitude families, so adjustment opens rather than closes the noncausal path.

variables.name: Societal-Norm Attitudes (A)
variables.content: Attitudes that influence both smoking and seat-belt use.

variables.name: Seat-Belt Usage (B)
variables.content: An observed collider influenced by both attitude families.

variables.name: Safety and Health Attitudes (C)
variables.content: Attitudes and measures influencing seat-belt use and lung disease.

variables.name: Lung Disease (Y)
variables.content: The outcome; this simplified graph contains no causal path from X.

arrows.because: Societal-norm attitudes can influence smoking behavior.
The same attitudes can influence seat-belt usage.
Safety and health attitudes also influence seat-belt usage.
Some health-related attitudes or traits affect susceptibility to lung disease.
